A working electric motor takes a current of 1.5 A when the p.d across it is 250V. If its efficiency is 80%, the power output is
questions.explanation: Input power = IV = 1.5 × 250 = 375 W. Efficiency = (output/input) × 100% → 80 = (output/375) × 100 → output = 300 W.

questions.question: The cost of running five 60 W lamps and four 100 W lamps for 20 hours if electrical energy cost #10.00 per kwh is
In a Daniel cell, the depolarizer, positive and negative electrodes are respectively
options: sulphuric acid, lead oxide and lead
questions.explanation: In a Daniel cell: depolarizer = copper sulphate solution, positive electrode = copper, negative electrode = zinc.

questions.question: When a piece of rectangular glass block is inserted between two parallel capacitor plates, at constant plate area and distance of separation, the capacitance of the capacitor will
questions.explanation: Inserting a dielectric (glass) increases the permittivity between the plates. Since C = kε₀A/d, capacitance increases.

questions.question: The ratio of electrostatic force F<sub>E</sub> to gravitational force F<sub>G</sub> between two protons each of charge e and mass m, at a distance d is
questions.explanation: FE = e²/(4πε₀d²). FG = Gm²/d². Ratio = [e²/(4πε₀d²)] ÷ [Gm²/d²] = e²/(4πε₀Gm²).

questions.question: A cell can supply current of 0.4 A and 0.2 A through a 4.0Ω and 10.0Ω resistors respectively. This internal resistance of the cell is
The particles emitted when <sup>39</sup><sub>19</sub>K decays to <sup>39</sup><sub>19</sub>K is
questions.explanation: Since both mass number (39) and atomic number (19) remain unchanged, the emission must be a gamma ray (electromagnetic radiation with no mass or charge).

questions.question: I. Low pressure. II. High pressure. III. High p.d. IV. Low p.d. Which combination of the above is true of the conduction of electricity through gases?
questions.explanation: Gases conduct electricity at low pressure and high potential difference. So I and III.

questions.question: The current through a resistor in an a.c circuit is given as 2 sin wt. Determine the d.c. equivalent of the current
questions.explanation: Comparing I = 2 sin ωt with I = I₀ sin ωt, I₀ = 2 A. The d.c. equivalent is the r.m.s. value: Irms = I₀/√2 = 2/√2 = √2 A.

questions.question: The primary coil of a transformer has N turns and is connected to a 120 V a.c. power line. If the secondary coil has 1000 turns and a terminal voltage of 1200 volts, what is the value of N?
Which of the following metals will provide the greatest shield against ionizing radiation?
questions.explanation: Lead has high density and high atomic number, making it the most effective shield against ionizing radiation (especially gamma rays).

questions.question: The process of energy production in the sun is
questions.explanation: The sun produces energy by nuclear fusion, where hydrogen nuclei combine to form helium, releasing vast energy.

questions.question: At resonance, the phase angle in an a.c. circuit is
questions.explanation: At resonance, XL = XC, so the circuit behaves as purely resistive. The phase angle between current and voltage is 0°.

questions.question: The force on a current carrying conductor in a magnetic field is greatest when the
options: conductor makes an angle of 60° with the field
force is independent of the angles between the fields and the conductor
conductor is parallel with the field
conductor is at right angle with the field
questions.explanation: F = BIL sin θ. Maximum force occurs when θ = 90°, i.e., the conductor is at right angle to the field.

questions.question: A transistor functions mainly as a
questions.explanation: A transistor is primarily used as a switch and amplifier in electronic circuits.

questions.question: Energy losses through eddy currents are reduced by using
questions.explanation: Insulated soft iron wires (laminations) increase resistance to eddy currents, reducing energy losses.

questions.question: A capacitor of 20 x 10<sup>-12</sup>F and an inductor are joined in series. The value of the inductance that will give the circuit a resonance frequency of 200 kHz is
The magnetic force on a charged particle moving with velocity v is
options: proportional to both the magnitude of the charge and the velocity v
independent of the magnitude of the charge
proportional to the velocity v only
proportional to the magnitude of the charge only
questions.explanation: Magnetic force F = qvB sin θ. So F is proportional to both q and v.

questions.question: A copper cube weighs 0.25 N in air, 0.17N when completely immersed in paraffin oil and 0.15 N when completely immersed in water. The ratio of upthrust in oil to upthrust in water is
questions.explanation: Upthrust in oil = 0.25 − 0.17 = 0.08 N. Upthrust in water = 0.25 − 0.15 = 0.10 N. Ratio = 0.08:0.10 = 4:5.

questions.question: A wheel and axle is used to raise a load of 500 N by the application of an effort of 250 N. If the radii of the wheel and the axle are 0.4 m and 0.1 m respectively, the efficiency of the machine is

The hydrostatic blood pressure difference between the head and the feet of a boy standing straight is 1.65 x 10<sup>4</sup> Nm<sup>-2</sup>. Find the height of the boy. [Density of blood = 1.1 x 10<sup>3</sup> kgm<sup>-3</sup>, g = 10ms<sup>-2</sup>]

A body weighing 80N stands in an elevator that is about to move. The force exerted by floor on the body as the elevator moves upward with an acceleration of 5 ms<sup>-2</sup> is [g = 10ms<sup>-2</sup>]
questions.explanation: Mass m = W/g = 80/10 = 8 kg. Normal force N = m(g + a) = 8(10 + 5) = 8 × 15 = 120 N.

questions.question: If the distance between two suspended masses 10kg each is tripled, the gravitational force of attraction between them is reduced by
questions.explanation: F ∝ 1/r². If r → 3r, F' = F/9. So the force is reduced to one-ninth.

questions.question: Two forces each of 10N acts on a body, one towards the north and the other towards the east. The magnitude and the direction of the resultant force are
questions.explanation: Perpendicular forces: R = √(10² + 10²) = 10√2 N. Direction = 45° east of north (NE). So 10√2 N, 45°E.

questions.question: A particle in circular motion performs 30 oscillations in 6 seconds. Its angular velocity is
questions.explanation: Frequency f = 30/6 = 5 Hz. Angular velocity ω = 2πf = 2π × 5 = 10π rad/s.

questions.question: The effect of a particle in a fluid attaining its terminal velocity is that the
options: weight is equal to the retarding force
buoyancy force is equal to the viscous retarding force
buoyancy force is more than the weight of the fluid displaced
questions.explanation: At terminal velocity, the net force is zero: weight = upthrust + viscous drag. The closest option is that weight equals the total retarding force.

questions.question: A coin placed below a rectangular glass block of thickness 9cm and refractive index 1.5 is viewed vertically above the block. The apparent displacement of the coin is
questions.explanation: Refractive index n = real depth/apparent depth → 1.5 = 9/apparent depth → apparent depth = 9/1.5 = 6 cm. Displacement = real − apparent = 9 − 6 = 3 cm.

questions.question: The radiator of a motor car is cooled by
questions.explanation: The radiator is cooled by convection (air moving through the fins, aided by the fan).

questions.question: I. Temperature. II. Density of air molecules III. Pressure IV. Pitch. Which of the above will affect the velocity of sound in the air
questions.explanation: Velocity of sound in air depends on temperature (I) and density of air molecules (II). Pressure (III) does not affect it; pitch (IV) is a property of the sound, not the medium.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of stationary waves?
options: They are formed by two identical waves travelling in opposite directions
they can be transverse or longitudinal
The distance between two successive nodes is one wavelength
The antinode is a point of minimum displacement
questions.explanation: Stationary waves are formed by the superposition of two identical waves travelling in opposite directions.

questions.question: To produce an enlarged and erect image with a concave mirror, the object must be positioned
options: between the principal focus and the centre of curvature
between the principal focus and the pole
questions.explanation: A concave mirror produces a virtual, erect, magnified image when the object is placed between the principal focus and the pole.

questions.question: The property that is propagated in a traveling wave is
questions.explanation: A traveling wave propagates energy (and momentum) through the medium, not matter.

questions.question: Which of the following eye defects can be corrected using a cylindrical lens.
questions.explanation: Astigmatism is caused by uneven curvature of the cornea or lens and is corrected using a cylindrical lens.

questions.question: The time rate of loss of heat by a body is proportional to the
options: difference in temperature between the body and its surroundings
ratio of the temperature of the body to that of its surroundings
questions.explanation: Newton's law of cooling: rate of heat loss is proportional to the temperature difference between the body and its surroundings.

questions.question: If tension is maintained on a stretched string of length 0.6m, such that its fundamental frequency of 220Hz is excited, determine the velocity of the transverse wave in the string.
questions.explanation: For fundamental frequency: f₀ = v/(2L) → v = 2Lf₀ = 2 × 0.6 × 220 = 264 m/s.

questions.question: A concave mirror of radius of curvature 40 cm forms a real image twice as large as the object. The object distance is
Water is a poor thermometric liquid because it
questions.explanation: Water wets glass, causing the meniscus to be curved and making accurate readings difficult. It also has a non-linear expansion.

questions.question: A ray of light which strikes a glass slab from air at normal incidence passes through the slab
options: undeviated and undisplaced at a lower speed
deviated and undisplaced at a lower speed
deviated and displaced at a lower speed
undeviated and displaced at a faster speed
questions.explanation: At normal incidence (angle = 0°), the ray passes straight through without deviation or lateral displacement, but its speed is lower in the glass.

questions.question: Blowing air over a liquid aids evaporation by
questions.explanation: Blowing air removes the vapour above the liquid, decreasing the vapour pressure and allowing more molecules to escape.

questions.question: The phenomenon that makes sound persist when its source has been removed is known as
questions.explanation: Reverberation is the persistence of sound due to multiple reflections in an enclosed space after the source has stopped.

Vibration in a stretched spring cannot be polarized because they are
questions.explanation: Only transverse waves can be polarized. Vibrations in a stretched spring along its length are longitudinal, so they cannot be polarized.

questions.question: The diagram above shows the velocity-time graph of a vehicle. Its acceleration and retardation respectively are
questions.explanation: Acceleration = slope of OA = 80/20 = 4 m/s². Retardation = slope of BC = 80/40 = 2 m/s². So 4.0 m/s² and 2.0 m/s².

questions.question: The figure above represents a frictionless pulley system in which a weight W is in equilibrium with a weight of 40N. Find the value of W
questions.explanation: For a pulley system with V.R. = 2 (two supporting strings), W = 2 × 40 = 80 N.

questions.question: The diagram above shows a solid figure with base PQ and center of gravity G on an inclined plane. Which of the following statements is correct
options: The solid will fall over if the vertical line through G lies outside the base
The solid will fall over if the vertical line through G lies inside the base
The solid will not fall over if the vertical line through G lies outside the base
The solid can never fall over
questions.explanation: A body topples when the vertical line through its centre of gravity falls outside its base.

questions.question: The diagram above shows a lift pump with valves at P and Q. During a downward stroke of the piston
options: P is open while Q is closed
P is closed while Q is open
questions.explanation: During the downward stroke of a lift pump, the piston moves down, valve P (in the piston) opens while valve Q (at the bottom) closes. So P is open while Q is closed.

questions.question: In the J-tube above, Y and X are on the same horizontal level and 30cm³ of air is trapped above Y when the atmospheric pressure is 75cm Hg, calculate the volume of air trapped above Y when 15cm Hg is now poured into the limb above X
questions.explanation: Using Boyle's law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂. P₁ = 75 cmHg, V₁ = 30 cm³. P₂ = 75 + 15 = 90 cmHg. V₂ = (75 × 30)/90 = 2250/90 = 25 cm³.

questions.question: The diagram above represents a transverse electromagnetic wave travelling with speed 3.0 x 10<sup>8</sup>ms<sup>-1</sup>. What is the frequency of the wave.
questions.explanation: From the diagram, total distance for 3 wavelengths = 0.3 m, so λ = 0.1 m. f = v/λ = (3.0×108)/0.1 = 3.0 × 109 Hz.

questions.question: The diagram above shows the prism arrangement in a
questions.explanation: The prism arrangement shown (two prisms at 45°) is used in a periscope to bend light by total internal reflection.

questions.question: The diagram above shows a magnet X with its south pole moved along a soft-iron bar PQ in the direction shown. After some time, the poles at P and Q respectively are
questions.explanation: When the south pole of a magnet approaches P, it induces a north pole at P (by magnetic induction). By conservation of magnetic flux, Q becomes a south pole. So P = North, Q = South.

In the circuit above, the potential across each capacitor is 100V. The total energy stored in the two capacitors is

questions.question: In the diagram above, if the internal resistance of the cell is zero, the ratio of the powers P₁ and P₂ dissipated by R₁ and R₂ is
questions.explanation: Power P = V²/R. Since the same voltage V is across both resistors (parallel), P₁ = V²/R₁ and P₂ = V²/R₂. Ratio P₁:P₂ = R₂:R₁ = R₂/R₁.

questions.question: In the series a.c circuit shown above, the p.d across the inductor is 8V<sub>r.m.s</sub> and that across the resistor is 6V<sub>r.m.s</sub>. The effective voltage is
questions.explanation: Effective voltage V = √(VR² + VL²) = √(6² + 8²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10 V.

questions.question: The velocity y of a particle in a time t is given by the equation y = 10 + 2t². Find the instantaneous acceleration after 5 seconds
questions.explanation: Acceleration a = dv/dt = d(10 + 2t²)/dt = 4t. At t = 5 s, a = 4 × 5 = 20 m/s².

questions.explanation: f ∝ √T. If T is doubled, f' = f₀√2 = f₀√2.

An engineer intends to deviate a light ray from its path by 120° through reflection from a plane mirror. Calculate the angle of incidence
questions.explanation: Angle of deviation = 180° − 2i. 120 = 180 − 2i → 2i = 60 → i = 30°.

questions.question: The diagram above shows a maximum and minimum thermometer divided into three portions P, Q and R. Which of the following is true about the respective content of P, Q and R
questions.explanation: In a maximum-minimum thermometer, the portions are filled with alcohol, mercury, and alcohol respectively (P = alcohol, Q = mercury, R = alcohol).

questions.question: The diagram above shows two capacitors P and Q of capacitance 5μF and 10μF. Find the charges stored in P and Q respectively
questions.explanation: Since they are in parallel, voltage across each = 20 V. QP = CPV = 5×10-6 × 20 = 100 μC. QQ = 10×10-6 × 20 = 200 μC.

questions.question: In the diagram above a beam of white light travels from a rare to a dense medium. What colours of light do the rays a, b and c respectively represents?
questions.explanation: In dispersion, shorter wavelengths (blue) bend more than longer wavelengths (red). The ray that bends least (a) is red, the middle (b) is green, and the one that bends most (c) is blue.

questions.question: In the diagram above, the values of V₁ and V₂ are respectively

questions.question: The correct position for a fuse in the diagram above is
questions.explanation: A fuse should be placed in the live (phase) wire to protect the circuit. In the diagram, the correct position is P.

questions.question: If current flows in the direction of the arrows in the solenoid above, the north pole is at

questions.explanation: Resonance occurs when the driving frequency matches the natural frequency. Pendulum T has the same length as P, so it will resonate with P.

questions.question: The diagram above is a block and tackle pulley system in which an effort of 80N is used to lift a load of 240N. The efficiency of the machine is
questions.explanation: M.A. = Load/Effort = 240/80 = 3. V.R. = number of pulleys = 6. Efficiency = M.A./V.R. × 100% = 3/6 × 100% = 50%.

questions.question: If ray travelling in air is incident on a transparent medium as shown in the diagram, the refractive index of the medium is given as
questions.explanation: Angle of incidence i = 90° − α. Refractive index n = sin i/sin r = sin(90° − α)/sin β = cos α/sin β.

questions.question: The diagram above shows two capacitors P and Q of capacitance 2μF and 4μF respectively connected to a d.c source. The ratio of energy stored in P to Q is
questions.explanation: Since they are in parallel, V is the same. Energy = ½CV². Ratio EP:EQ = CP:CQ = 2:4 = 1:2.

The diagram above shows a closed cube of side 0.5m in a uniform electric field E in the direction shown by the arrows. What is the flux Φ for the box?
questions.explanation: For a closed surface in a uniform electric field, the total flux is zero because the flux entering equals the flux leaving. So Φ = 0.0 E.

questions.question: The diagram above shows the force (F) acting on an object through a distance (x). The work done on this object is expressed as
questions.explanation: Work done = area under force-distance graph = area of triangle = ½ × F × x = Fx/2 J.

questions.question: The energy stored in a capacitor of capacitance 10μF carrying a charge of 100μC is
When connected to a mains of 250V, the fuse rating in the plug of an electric device of 1 KW is
questions.explanation: Current I = P/V = 1000/250 = 4 A. For safety, fuse rating should be ~125% of operating current: 4 × 1.25 = 5 A. So 5 A.

questions.question: The eye controls the amount of light reaching the retina by adjusting the
questions.explanation: The iris controls the size of the pupil, thereby regulating the amount of light entering the eye.

questions.question: An electric iron is rated 1000W, 230V. What is the resistance of its elements?

options: Both X and Y are negative
Both X and Y are positive
X is positive and Y is negative
X is negative and Y is positive
questions.explanation: The field lines point away from both X and Y, indicating that both are positive charges.

questions.question: The electromagnetic wave that can produce a heating effect on the environment is
questions.explanation: Infrared rays are strongly absorbed by most materials and produce a heating effect (thermal radiation).

questions.question: An electric cell with nominal voltage E has a resistance of 3Ω connected across it. If the voltage falls to 0.6E, the internal resistance of the cell is
<sup>23</sup><sub>11</sub>Na + X → <sup>20</sup><sub>9</sub>F + <sup>4</sup><sub>2</sub>He. What particle is X in the reaction above?
questions.explanation: Balancing: mass number: 23 + A = 20 + 4 → A = 1. Atomic number: 11 + Z = 9 + 2 → Z = 0. So X is a neutron (10n).

questions.question: Pure silicon can be converted to a p-type by adding a controlled amount of
questions.explanation: Adding trivalent atoms (e.g., boron) creates holes, making silicon p-type.

questions.question: The energy associated with the photon of a radio transmission at 3 x 10<sup>5</sup> Hz is [h = 6.63 x 10<sup>-34</sup>Js]
The percentage of the original nuclei of the sample of a radioactive substance left after 5 half-lives is
questions.explanation: Fraction remaining = (1/2)5 = 1/32. Percentage = 1/32 × 100% = 3.125% ≈ 3%.

questions.question: From the generating station to each substation power is transmitted at a very high voltage so as to reduce
questions.explanation: High voltage reduces current for the same power. Since power loss = I²R, lower current means less heating in the coils.

questions.question: The particle that is responsible for the nuclear fission in a nuclear reactor is
questions.explanation: Neutrons are used to bombard heavy nuclei (e.g., U-235) to trigger fission, as they are neutral and can penetrate the nucleus easily.

questions.question: A transistor is used in the amplification of signals because it

questions.question: A bead travelling on a straight line wire is brought to rest at 0.2m by friction. If the mass of the bead is 0.01kg and the coefficient of friction between the bead and the wire is 0.1, determine the work done by the friction [g = 10ms<sup>-2</sup>]
questions.explanation: Friction force F = μmg = 0.1 × 0.01 × 10 = 0.01 N. Work done = F × d = 0.01 × 0.2 = 0.002 = 2 × 10-3 J.

questions.question: On top of a spiral spring of the force constant 500Nm<sup>-1</sup> is placed a mass of 5 x 10<sup>-3</sup> kg. If the spring is compressed downwards by a length of 0.02m and then released, calculate the height to which the mass is projected
questions.explanation: Energy stored = ½ke² = ½ × 500 × (0.02)² = 0.1 J. This converts to gravitational P.E.: mgh = 0.1 → (5×10-3 × 10)h = 0.1 → 0.05h = 0.1 → h = 2 m.

questions.question: A test tube of radius 1.0cm is loaded to 8.8g. If it is placed upright in water, find the depth to which it would sink
questions.explanation: Weight of test tube = mg = 0.0088 × 10 = 0.088 N. Buoyancy = ρgπr²h = 1000 × 10 × π × (0.01)² × h = 3.142h. Equating: 3.142h = 0.088 → h = 0.028 m = 2.8 cm.

questions.question: A 90cm uniform lever has a load of 30N suspended at 15cm from one of its ends. If the fulcrum is at the center of gravity, the force that must be applied at its other end to keep it in horizontal equilibrium is
questions.explanation: Fulcrum at center = 45 cm mark. Load at 15 cm mark is 30 cm from fulcrum. Let F be applied at the other end (90 cm mark), which is 45 cm from fulcrum. Taking moments: F × 45 = 30 × 30 → F = 900/45 = 20 N.
